extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of literature; literary critics and critics-in-training
extracted.subtask_short: criticism of modern poetry and prose
extracted.subtask_description: Critical evaluation of modern European literature (exemplified by Goethe and Heine), focusing on originality, application of ideas, style, form, and the writer's relation to society (e.g., Philistinism).

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist must work from within outwards
rubrics_metrics.description: "as man must live from within outwards, so the artist must work from within outwards, seeing that, make what contortions he will, he can only bring to light his own individuality." (Goethe)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality is judged by the degree to which the artist's individuality is expressed rather than by conformity to external rules or fashions. Anti-pattern: trying to manufacture originality by following external prescriptions or imitating dominant forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profound imperturbable naturalism / standard inside every man
rubrics_metrics.description: "Goethe's profound, imperturbable naturalism... he puts the standard, once for all, inside every man instead of outside him; when he is told, such a thing must be so... he answers... 'But _is_ it so? is it so to _me_?'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical criterion: does the work locate its standards internally (authentic reaction, personal truth) rather than appealing to authority, custom, or received opinion? Anti-pattern: deference to authority or custom without personal verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry as the most effective mode for influence
rubrics_metrics.description: "Poetry is simply the most beautiful, impressive, and widely effective mode of saying things, and hence its importance."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a poet or deciding form, consider poetry's disproportionate power to 'secure the ear of the world' — i.e., the capacity to influence taste and thought. Use poetic form when broad persuasive or affective reach is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature's function: apply modern ideas to life, not direct political action
rubrics_metrics.description: "Direct political action is not the true function of literature... Heine was a born man of letters... his propagandism took another, a more truly literary, character."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess literary work by how effectively it embodies and applies ideas in the realm of culture and imagination rather than by immediate political agitation. Anti-pattern: expecting literature to perform as party politics rather than as a vehicle for ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attack Philistinism — value ideas over mere practical conveniences
rubrics_metrics.description: Heine's battle with Philistinism: "the enthusiast for the idea... values reason, the idea, in and for themselves; the man who regards the possession of... practical conveniences as something sufficient... is, in his eyes, a Philistine."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A writer is judged by whether they champion ideas intrinsically (intellectual courage and commitment) rather than placating or celebrating mere practical success. Anti-pattern: treating ideas as instruments or tokens to be traded off against comfort or convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply ideas with freedom, clearness, and originality
rubrics_metrics.description: "He exhibited in literature modern ideas applied with the utmost freedom, clearness, and originality."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: ideas must be not only present but actively and originally applied to subjects and life with clarity and independence. Anti-pattern: abundance of ideas without practical or textual application (ideas as 'counters' or 'marbles').

rubrics_metrics.name: Blend clearness and lightness with power of feeling and width of range
rubrics_metrics.description: "Wonderful clearness, lightness, and freedom, united with such power of feeling, and width of range."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate style by the successful union of lucid, economical expression (French modernism) with depth of feeling and expansive intellectual range (German tradition). Weakness arises when one pole dominates to the exclusion of the other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mingle wit and pathos; combine prose and verse effectively
rubrics_metrics.description: "Prose and verse, wit and seriousness, are mingled in [Reisebilder], and the mingling of these is characteristic of Heine."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successful modern writer can fuse humor and seriousness and traverse forms (prose/verse) so that each enhances the other's effect. Anti-pattern: tonal monotony or an inability to hold juxtaposed modes together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use popular/formal forms (ballad-form) with rapidity, grace, and pathos
rubrics_metrics.description: "He chiefly uses a form of old German popular poetry, a ballad-form which has more rapidity and grace... he employs this form with the most exquisite lightness and ease, and yet it has at the same time the inborn fulness, pathos, and old-world charm of all true forms of popular poetry."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: choice and mastery of form — traditional or popular forms can be powerful if used with skill, lightness, and genuine feeling. Anti-pattern: mechanical use of form without ease or authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject stock classicism and stock romanticism; maintain absolute freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: "His absolute freedom, his utter rejection of stock classicism and stock romanticism..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value originality and independence from received stylistic orthodoxies. Anti-pattern: derivative writing that simply recycles classicist or romantic clichés.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain authorial voice; avoid 'beautifully objective' impersonation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Never does Heine attempt to be _hubsch objectiv_... he always remains Heinrich Heine, a son of the nineteenth century."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When handling historical or varied subjects, a strength is to retain a distinctive contemporary voice rather than attempting to impersonate other eras or personae 'beautifully objectively.' Anti-pattern: losing authorial presence in forced objectivity or pastiche.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musical rhythm and accessibility of verse
rubrics_metrics.description: Praise for Heine's rhythms: contrasted awkward foreign rhythms with satisfying lines like 'Take, oh, take those lips away...' — "The magic of Heine's poetical form is incomparable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess verse for rhythm and musicality that resonates with readers (including cross-linguistic considerations). Anti-pattern: prosody that alienates or is awkward in the reader's idiom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth must be unified by a strong central idea
rubrics_metrics.description: "Wide, so impartial, that it is apt to become slack and powerless, and to lose itself in its materials for want of a strong central idea round which to group all its other ideas."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: intellectual breadth is a virtue only when organized by a central, unifying idea; otherwise the work risks diffuseness. Anti-pattern: vast erudition without organizing principle.
